When we picked rooms I picked first because I moved in first and then my roommate upstairs picked and then the girl downstairs. She wasn’t too happy with her room because it was the smallest and the location but settled because she had her own bathroom. So the roommate downstairs has a very weird schedule. Sometimes she works nights and sometimes mornings. Sometimes she has 5 hour days and other days she can work 13. So obviously with the constant changing work schedule her sleeping schedule has became very weird and erratic and we never know when she’s asleep now. So since I can never guess when she’s asleep I often so downstairs in the kitchen and make food and play music on my speaker while I meal prep. It’s apart of my routine through out the day that i really enjoy since I don’t work till 2pm. She said it wakes her up almost every time and when she is a wake it’s just very disruptive. My other roommate said sure but I said that’s not really fair because she often plays music too in the kitchen. She told me it wasn’t really fair that she had the shittiest room in the house and that if I wanted to switch with her so she wouldn’t have to be woken up by it that would be fine. Of course I said no and said I was going to keep playing music because it’s noon usually when I do it and it’s ridiculous I have to step around her schedule. Both my roommates are saying I’m being an asshole and that it’s the least I can do because I have the best room in the house because it’s the most separate. I honestly think they are being assholes because why should I have to be so quiet I’m the middle of the day!?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I need to figure out if the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person is a man living in a duplex with two other girls. The layout is such that there are two bedrooms upstairs sharing a bathroom, and downstairs there's a living room, kitchen, dining room, and another room with its own bathroom. When they moved in, he picked first, then the other roommate upstairs, and the last roommate took the smallest room downstairs but had her own bathroom.

The roommate downstairs has a weird sleep schedule because of her varying work hours. Sometimes she works nights, sometimes mornings, and her days can be as short as 5 hours or as long as 13. Because of this, her sleeping schedule is erratic, and they never know when she's asleep.

The man often goes downstairs to the kitchen to make food and play music on his speaker as part of his routine. He doesn't work until 2 pm, so he has the time. However, the roommate downstairs messaged the group chat asking them to stop playing music at any time of the day because it wakes her up and is disruptive.

The other roommate agreed, but the man refused, saying it's not fair because the roommate downstairs often plays music too. He also mentioned that she has the worst room in the house and suggested switching rooms if she wants to avoid being woken up. He refused to switch and continued playing music, arguing that it's noon and unreasonable to have to adjust his routine around her schedule.

Both roommates are calling him an asshole, saying it's the least he can do because he has the best room. He thinks they're being assholes because he shouldn't have to be so quiet in the middle of the day.

Now, I need to evaluate whether his action is morally acceptable. Let's break it down.

First, the roommate downstairs has a very irregular sleep schedule due to her work. This means she might be sleeping during times when others are awake, including the middle of the day. The man is playing music in the kitchen, which is a common area, and this is disturbing her sleep.

He argues that she also plays music in the kitchen, so it's not fair for her to ask him to stop. However, the fact that she plays music doesn't necessarily mean it's okay for him to do the same, especially if it's disruptive to her. Also, he mentions that she has the smallest room, which might be noisier or less private, but that doesn't excuse him from being considerate of her need to sleep.

He also suggests switching rooms, but when she offers, he refuses. This shows that he's not willing to compromise or find a solution that accommodates both their needs. Instead, he insists on continuing his routine, which is causing a problem for her.

In a shared living situation, mutual respect and consideration are important. If one person's actions are consistently disturbing another's ability to rest, it's reasonable for the disturbed party to ask for adjustments. The man's refusal to stop playing music, especially when it's causing a problem, could be seen as inconsiderate and self-centered.

Moreover, he's in a better room, which might mean he has more privacy or a quieter space. It's not unreasonable for the others to ask him to be more considerate, especially since he's in a position where he can afford to be quieter without as much disturbance.

So, considering all this, his action of continuing to play music despite the disturbance seems morally unacceptable because it's inconsiderate of his roommate's needs and disrupts her ability to rest, which is a basic necessity, especially given her erratic schedule.
